name: SC-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Timmons with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: The R+11 district, Timmons's incumbency and dominant fundraising advantage, and Polymarket pricing near 94% Republican all point to a comfortable hold, with no polls or ratings suggesting a competitive race. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly -15.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Timmons showing the race narrowing would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, and incumbent William Timmons is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. Democrat Courtney McClain has run a minimal campaign, raising about $33,000 with little cash on hand, while Timmons has raised roughly $1.6 million and drawn nearly $500,000 in outside support. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is not a factor.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Timmons about a 94% chance of winning. The expected margin is roughly fifteen points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling, but the seat is very likely to stay in Republican hands.
